ruling.recommended_action: Refund $5.89 excess distance fare to the rider's original payment method; log the uninformed-reroute notification failure on the driver's route compliance record and issue the driver a notification-duty reminder (no formal warning, first such incident).
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen first: the chat (F7–F9), the complaint and the driver's statement (F10) contain no threat, harassment, sexual remark, dangerous-driving or accident allegation. "Uncle … you decide" is a pickup/routing remark, not a safety indicator. safety_concern = none.

Route deviation: F1 shows actual 14.9 km vs optimal 10.7 km = +4.2 km, well over the 1 km tolerance (RD-1). The single off-route segment, 21:43–21:50 (F3), drove Jalan Bukit Merah → Kampong Bahru Road → Telok Blangah Road → Henderson Road, covering 5.14 km where the optimal route covers 1.44 km, adding 3.70 km; no 0.2 km noise issue.

Is the segment exempt? The rider never named a road or place; she gave a blanket "any way also can, you decide" (F7) — general, unnamed route discretion. RD-5's consent branch requires the rider to have agreed to go via a named road; where an agreed route has no road names in the record the system default is to escalate, but here there is no agreement to a specific route at all: a content-free "you decide" does not convert the driver's own choice of off-route roads into the rider's route under RD-3. The rider's own complaint confirms she did not know the roads and did not ask for Bukit Merah/Kampong Bahru/Telok Blangah/Henderson. So the segment counts.

Traffic: no exemption under RD-4 — the AYE was at speed band 7 (60–69 km/h, F11) and the CTE band 8 (F12), and no incident is recorded (F13); a segment is traffic-justified only on a closure/incident or speed band 1–2. F13/F14 confirm none.

Notice/consent (RD-5): the driver's only on-trip message was "Ok auntie, no problem" at 21:38 (F8), before/at the start of the trip — no statement that he would leave the expressway and go via Bukit Merah/Kampong Bahru/Telok Blangah/Henderson, and no reason given. The rider effectively learned of the route only from the fare. His post-trip statement (F10) that she said "any way can" is a claim, not consent to a specific route, and is in any case not notice. No call recording is in the record.

Amount: no exempt km, so refundable km = the excess. The fare record gives the excess directly: $5.89 (4.18 km × this trip's per-km distance fare $1.4098) [F4]. Tolls, time fare and surge are not refunded; surge is 1.0× (F5), so nothing to add. Rider's claimed "extra" ($5.89) matches the recorded excess, so refund_partial = $5.89.

Repeat-deviation flag (RD-6): the driver has 3 disputes and 2 upheld, but 0 upheld route deviations (F16) — no upheld route deviation in the last 90 days, so flag_account is not triggered and F16 does not decide this case (profile facts never decide alone).

Precedent: DISP-001 (uninformed reroute, excess distance fare refunded at the trip's per-km rate) and DISP-2026-0089 (uninformed reroute, $3.20) align: refund the excess distance fare. RD-7 also requires the notification reminder and compliance log entry. Amount is under $10, so the system ruling is final (TH-1; C1).

segment_findings.reason: Off-route segment 21:43–21:50 drove Jalan Bukit Merah → Kampong Bahru Road → Telok Blangah Road → Henderson Road, +3.70 km. The rider named no place or road and gave only a blank 'any way also can, you decide' (F7); there was no agreement to a specific named road, so RD-5/RD-3 do not exempt the segment, and the driver's own selection of these roads is not the rider's route. No RD-4 traffic reason: AYE band 7 (60–69 km/h, F11), CTE band 8 (F12), no incident (F13). Driver's notice (F8) was a bare 'Ok auntie, no problem' with no mention of the reroute; his post-trip claim of blanket permission (F10) is not notice or consent to a named route. Segment counts under RD-2.

element_findings.reason: AYE speed band 7 (60–69 km/h) and CTE band 8 (70+ km/h) during the trip window; no incident recorded. Neither a closure/incident nor a band 1–2 condition is present, so RD-4 gives no exemption.

element_findings.element: Rider agreement to a named route/road (RD-5 / RD-3)
element_findings.reason: Rider's 21:38 message named no road or place and merely deferred to the driver ('any way also can, you decide'); a general unnamed discretion is not agreement to the Bukit Merah/Kampong Bahru/Telok Blangah/Henderson routing the driver actually took.

element_findings.element: Driver notice before/at the point of deviation (RD-5)
element_findings.reason: The only driver message (F8) is 'Ok auntie, no problem' with no reason and no mention of the reroute; the statement about 'any way can' (F10) was written after the trip and is a claim, not contemporaneous notice, and no call recording exists.

element_findings.element: Repeat driver route deviation within 90 days (RD-6)
element_findings.reason: Driver profile shows 2 upheld disputes but 0 upheld route deviations, so no repeat-deviation flag is added; profile never decides the case.

rejected_claims.reason: The rider's 'any way also can, you decide' (F7) is a blanket unnamed discretion given by a rider who said she did not know the roads; it does not equal agreement to the driver's specific off-expressway route via Bukit Merah/Kampong Bahru/Telok Blangah/Henderson (F3). The driver's post-trip statement (F10) is a claim, not consent, and system records (F1, F3) show the deviation.

No RD-4 basis: AYE band 7 and CTE band 8 with no incident (F11–F13) means no closure, incident or congestion condition on the replaced part of the recommended route; slow-but-free-flowing expressway is not a traffic reason to divert.
